The clone is done. `clone.html` is written to the required path, with `original.png` and `clone-round1.png` screenshots saved alongside it (plus two throwaway center-crop attempts that didn't help, left in place).

**Summary of decisions:**

- **Source has zero CSS.** The fixture page (`page.html`) is just semantic markup — an `<h1>` and three `.testimonial-card` divs, no `<style>` tag or stylesheet link anywhere. So there's no author-defined theme (colors, spacing, layout) to extract; the entire visual appearance is the browser's default UA stylesheet (white background, black text, bold `<h1>` at ~2em, default paragraph margins, left-aligned block flow).
- **Componentized `.testimonial-card`** as the one reusable unit (avatar image + quote), since the class name and repetition (×3) clearly signal intentional structure, even though no styling is attached to it yet. Kept the div/img/p structure and class name verbatim rather than inventing card chrome (borders, shadows, padding) that isn't in the source.
- **Text transcribed verbatim** from the fetched HTML: heading "What people say," all three alt attributes ("Avatar for Jamie Wren," etc.), and all three quotes, copied exactly rather than paraphrased.
- **Images**: the source references root-relative paths (`/avatar-1.jpg`, `/avatar-2.jpg`, `/avatar-3.jpg`) that don't resolve to anything even in the original fixture (no real domain, no local file). Per the hotlink-don't-fabricate rule, I left these paths exactly as authored rather than inventing a fake host or placeholder — both original and clone render them as broken/missing images identically.
- **Tailwind CDN** loaded per the required approach; since there's no bespoke design tokens to extend, I only used `tailwind.config` to encode the two default UA values Tailwind's preflight reset would otherwise strip (`h1`'s `2em`/`bold`/`0.67em` margin, and paragraph `1em` margins), so the page matches default browser typography instead of Tailwind's reset flattening it.
- **Nothing flagged as unrecreatable** — this fixture has no JS-driven widgets, carousels, or lazy content to worry about.
- **Screenshot comparison**: took one original (1280×900) and one clone screenshot at the same viewport. Side-by-side they match closely — same heading size/weight/position, same stacked card layout, same broken-image/alt-text presentation, same paragraph spacing and body margin. Given the simplicity (no color, no layout complexity), one round was sufficient rather than forcing extra iterations for no gain.
